newsitem.title: USA: Bank of New York, NationsBank profits up in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New York, NationsBank profits up in quarter.

text.p: NationsBank Corp. said Monday its profits rose strongly in the first quarter, helped by productivity improvements, while Bank of New York reported a more modest gain in earnings.
Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank said its earnings rose 38 percent to $709 million in the first quarter from $513 million in the year-ago quarter.
Earnings per share rose to 97 cents from 85 cents, even after the issuance of new shares for the acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares, which was completed in January.

"This quarter was marked by continued focus on productivity initiatives and substantial progress on the integration of the former Boatmen's franchise," said NationsBank Chief Executive Hugh McColl Jr..
NationsBank, the nation's fourth largest bank in terms of assets, said its net interest income surged 25 percent to $1.98 billion in the first quarter.
Noninterest income rose 26 percent to $1.11 billion, mainly boosted by deposit accounts and asset management and fiduciary service fees.
The Bank of New York said its profits rose in the first quarter as a drop in interest income was offset by strong gains in fees, and foreign exchange and other trading activities.

Bank of New York, ranked 16th in terms of assets, said its earnings rose to $265 million in the first quarter from $243 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per rose to 65 cents from 58 cents, above the 63 cents consensus estimate on Wall Street.

The Bank of New York said its net interest income fell to $496 million from $521 million for the 1996 first quarter, after it sold about $900 million in credit card receivables to Associates National Bank, as of Jan. 1, 1997.
Total noninterest income rose to $455 million from $415 million. Revenues from foreign exchange and other trading activities shot up to $27 million in the quarter from $10 million a year earlier.
Securities processing fees increased 16 percent to $185 million. The company reported $7 million of securities gains in the quarter vs. $33 million a year ago.
